title: Simplex result reset
summary: Recovered the no-argument thiscall reset at VA 0x546100: clear status at +0x24, zero four float weights at +0x14 through +0x20, and clear only flags bits 0..3 at +0x10. Preserve all other object bytes. Caller at 0x546374 supplies a result subobject at simplex+0x13c and subsequently assigns weight zero to 1.0f. Implementation is a genuine member method compatible with GCC and MSVC2013.
test_description: GCC i386 freestanding harness directly compares the member method to the byte-verified original at 0x546100 for every 16-bit flags value, with cycling byte patterns covering every old status and weight byte value. Independent expected-byte checks cover exact write footprint, prefix, reserved bytes, trailing padding and surrounding guards. Repeated resets verify idempotence. Initialized test-owned FS storage is installed successfully and its head checked after every original call. Local run passes; optional pinned MSVC2013 O2 compilation succeeds.
known_limits: Original field/debug names, meanings of preserved high flag bits, prefix contents and status semantics remain unresolved; weights are inferred from caller floating-point use.
Only offsets through 0x24 are proven; the modeled 0x28 size includes natural alignment padding and does not establish complete original object extent.
Valid writable objects are required; null, dangling, inaccessible or misaligned objects and concurrent access are outside the C++ contract.
Incidental EAX value and CPU condition flags are not modeled as a return contract. No compiler-byte matching is claimed.
